speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have knee pain after increased physical activity; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Given the history of repetitive pivoting and twisting in volleyball, is there a "pop" you heard or felt at the onset of the pain, and do you have any significant swelling or instability in the knee?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints). The pain location (medial tibia, inferior to patella) combined with recent increased physical activity and weight loss attempts is classic for this condition; I will not request further tests as the clinical picture is sufficient.
